summary: Discovery call to evaluate migrating Elysium's production LLM traffic from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated. Covered current stack (OpenAI + vLLM for local ops), performance expectations, compatibility concerns (tokenization, model variants, vLLM/TGI integration), security (SAML, KMS, SOC2), and next steps: pricing, benchmark run, and a 2-week Dedicated trial. Customer is price-sensitive but needs parity on output quality and auditability for healthcare data.

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-04 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Ari Stein (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam Carter (Elysium CTO), Priya Nair (ML Eng), Diego Ramos (SecOps)

Auto-generated summary: Discussed migration path from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated, compatibility questions re: vLLM/TGI, and pilot plan.

00:00 Ari Stein: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros?
00:10 Liam Carter: Hey, Liam here, CTO at Elysium. we run most prod calls through OpenAI today, we also run some local inference with vLLM for batch jobs.
00:20 Priya Nair: Priya, ML eng, I own the model infra and pipeline.
00:25 Diego Ramos: Diego, SecOps. I'll be owning the security checklist.
00:30 Ari Stein: Great. Maya, do you want to do a quick Redwood overview?
00:35 Maya Chen: Sure. Redwood provides hosted and dedicated inference. for dedicated you get reserved GPU pools, private network options, KMS integration, audit logs, and we focus on matching latency and eval parity. we also have smart routing so you can fall back to hosted if needed.
00:55 Liam Carter: Quick context: our main concern is twofold - cost and control. OpenAI is convenient but cost is rising. for some internal batch scoring we use vLLM/TGI; we need the model outputs to match production behavior.
01:15 Priya Nair: yeah, tokenization differences killed us before - small prompt reformats gave different answers across runtimes.
01:30 Maya Chen: totally, that's a common issue. when you move runtimes you can hit tokenizer or model variant mismatches. Redwood has tooling to pin model versions, and we provide tokenization sanity checks and a small eval harness to compare outputs.
01:50 Diego Ramos: security - we need SOC2, SSO via SAML/Okta, HSM/KMS for keys, and audit logs retained for 12 months. also data residency matters for some datasets.
02:10 Ari Stein: We support SOC2 and have customers in healthcare. SAML/Okta yes, and KMS integrations - we can support AWS & GCP KMS. our Private option can be deployed in a VPC or on-prem if needed.
02:40 Liam Carter: good. on performance, our SLO is 200ms 95 p99 maybe 500ms. current p95 on OpenAI is around 150ms but network overhead is variable.
03:05 Maya Chen: For Dedicated we size the cluster by peak QPS and model. we often recommend X GPUs for low latency gen models. we do KV cache + prefix caching to reduce per-token compute for repeated contexts. that helps your 95th percentile.
03:30 Priya Nair: how does Redwood handle batching? our batch jobs use TGI for large-batch throughput.
03:40 Maya Chen: Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and per-tenant policies. for throughput jobs, we can tune batching windows; for latency-sensitive endpoints we set smaller windows. we also support quantized kernels - a tradeoff between quality and cost.
04:05 Liam Carter: hmm, about eval parity - will Redwood's dedicated run produce identical generations to OpenAI? we can't have regressions in clinical phrasing.
04:20 Maya Chen: Short answer: we aim for parity but exact token-for-token identity isn't guaranteed across different model weights/providers. if you're using OpenAI's proprietary models, parity depends on running the same model artifacts. if you run open weights (e.g., Llama-derivatives) we can often match. we can run an eval suite to measure deltas and tune temperature, sampling, quantization to get within your thresholds.
04:55 Priya Nair: For the parts we run locally with vLLM/TGI, how does Redwood integrate? can we bring our vLLM config?
05:10 Maya Chen: Redwood can integrate with vLLM/TGI stacks in two ways: you can keep your local vLLM for batch processing and route prod traffic to Redwood Dedicated, or we can run the same runtime inside Dedicated if you want a single control plane. there are some nuances: support for kernel-level ops, custom kernels, and kv-cache implementations vary, so we test those in the bench.
05:40 Diego Ramos: is there support for private connectivity - like a VPC peering and no public ingress?
05:50 Ari Stein: yes, Dedicated supports VPC-only endpoints and we offer a Private deployment for fully customer-controlled control plane.
06:05 Liam Carter: pricing - high level? we spend X on tokens today; curious on committed vs burst.
06:15 Ari Stein: We'll send a committed capacity quote; typically reserved capacity + burst buffer. pricing includes a baseline for GPUs and a per-token or per-output unit estimate. I'll attach a pricing spreadsheet after the call.
06:35 Priya Nair: on quantization - some of our models are sensitive; 4-bit quant caused hallucinations earlier.
06:45 Maya Chen: we track quality regressions tied to quant profiles. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles per workload; for clinical prompts we'd keep higher fidelity or run eval regression checks.
07:10 Liam Carter: what's the trial like? we'd want a short Dedicated pilot against a subset of traffic with benchmarks comparing OpenAI outputs.
07:20 Ari Stein: Typical pilot is 2 weeks: provision a small Dedicated cluster, run your eval set, measure latency/cost/quality. Maya will own the bench run.
07:35 Maya Chen: I'll provide a benchmark template. please send representative prompts and a sample of current logs (no PHI in test set unless it's approved).
07:50 Liam Carter: expected time to provision?
07:55 Ari Stein: usually 3-5 business days for Dedicated provisioning once contracts are in place; for trial we can expedite.
08:05 Diego Ramos: we need a security pack before we spin anything up - network diagram, pen test results, SOC2 docs.
08:15 Ari Stein: we'll send the pack.
08:20 Priya Nair: technical question: tokenizers - do you run the same tokenizer binaries as OpenAI?
08:30 Maya Chen: we run popular tokenizer libs, and we can vendor specific tokenizer versions. the bench includes tokenization parity checks. sometimes differences are due to normalization/whitespace; we canonicalize inputs in the harness.
08:55 Liam Carter: any gotchas with vLLM/TGI stateful KV caches? we've seen cache mismatch causing context skew.
09:10 Maya Chen: KV cache formats differ. we map and validate KV cache behavior; for continuous sessions we recommend Redwood's managed KV cache to ensure consistency. if you need to import vLLM caches, that's part of the bench work.
09:35 Priya Nair: do you support multi-model rollouts? we sometimes A/B between model variants.
09:45 Maya Chen: yes - canary deploys, A/B tests, automatic fallback. routing policies can be based on latency or cost.
10:05 Diego Ramos: questions on audit logs - format, retention, and access controls?
10:15 Ari Stein: logs are stored with RBAC; we can export in JSON (S3) and retain per contract. access via roles and SSO.
10:30 Liam Carter: okay, let's talk success criteria for pilot: 1) no more than 5% delta in clinical response metrics on eval set; 2) p95 latency within 200-250ms; 3) 20% cost reduction target.
10:50 Maya Chen: noted. we'll design the bench to measure those metrics.
11:05 Priya Nair: one more - model weights: will Redwood host open weights or do you provide conversions?
11:15 Maya Chen: we can host open weights. for proprietary OpenAI models we can't run them outside OpenAI; in that case we test by running comparable open models and measuring parity. if you license a model artifact we can deploy it in Dedicated.
11:40 Liam Carter: hmm, we do rely on some OpenAI specifics for fine-tuned endpoints.
11:50 Ari Stein: for fine-tuned models, we typically recommend exporting the fine-tuned checkpoint or running a compatibility eval.
12:05 Diego Ramos: legal/procurement timeline?
12:10 Liam Carter: procurement would like 4-6 weeks; security review in parallel.
12:20 Ari Stein: we can work with procurement and provide standard docs; if you need custom terms we can escalate.
12:35 Priya Nair: ok we've got the high level. next steps recap?
12:40 Ari Stein: I'll send pricing, SOC2/ISO certs, network diagram, and Maya will send the bench template. you (Liam) will share prompts and OpenAI usage export. we'll target provisioning trial by Mar 9 and a follow-up on Mar 11 to review bench results.
13:05 Liam Carter: that works. thanks everyone.
13:10 Diego Ramos: thanks.
13:15 Maya Chen: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
